facts.statement: Luanchuanraptor is known from a partial skeleton found in the Qiupa Formation of Henan, China.
facts.quote: The genus is based on a partial skeleton from the Qiupa Formation in Luanchuan, Henan.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as 41HIII-0100, was described by Lü and colleagues in 2007.
facts.quote: The fossils were cataloged as 41HIII-0100 and described by Lü and colleagues in 2007.

facts.statement: The fossil remains include the skull roof, neck and back vertebrae, tail bones, ribs, shoulder girdle, leg bones, and hand claws.
facts.quote: It consists of the left frontal, 4 teeth (9 were identified but 5 were excluded), 4 cervical vertebrae, 6 dorsal vertebrae, 17 caudal vertebrae, 4 ribs, 4 chevrons, a right humerus, left scapulocoracoid, the first phalanx from right manus, an isolated manual ungual, right ilium, left pubis, ischium, the sacrum and the shaft of the left femur.

facts.statement: This genus represents the first dromaeosaurid discovered in Asia outside of northeastern China or the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: Es el primer dromeosáurido encontrado en Asia fuera del noreste de China o el desierto de gobi.

facts.statement: Adult Luanchuanraptor are estimated to have been 1.1 to 1.8 meters long and weighed between 2.2 and 2.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Luanchuanraptor were moderate-sized dromaeosaurs, estimated at 1.1 to 1.8 m long with weights from 2.2 to 2.5 kg.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest Luanchuanraptor reached a height of 0.60 meters and a weight of approximately 12 kilograms.
facts.quote: El Luanchuanraptor henanensis es un dromeosáurido que se estima que llegó a medir 1,5 metros de largo y 0,60 de alto, pesando cerca de los 12 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Luanchuanraptor is distinguished by a stiff tail tip, short tail vertebrae spines, connected front tail chevrons, and a large opening in the shoulder bone.
facts.quote: They can be recognised from other dromaeosaur taxa in having a very stiff tail tip as indicated by the short neural spines of the caudal vertebrae, connected anterior chevrons, some posterior caudals with depressions near the neural spine, stocky proximal and posterior end of the chevrons, and a large opening on the coracoid.

facts.statement: Luanchuanraptor lived during the Late Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is considered to be Late Maastrichtian in age about 72 million to 66 million years ago based on stratigraphic correlations.

facts.statement: The species lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 84 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 84 y 71 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The habitat consisted of shallow lakes and braided delta rivers.
facts.quote: Most of the environments present consisted on shallow lakes with braided, delta rivers.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses classify Luanchuanraptor as a velociraptorine closely related to Adasaurus.
facts.quote: The recently performed phylogenetic analysis for the Dromaeosauridae by Hartman et al. 2019 recovers Luanchuanraptor as a velociraptorine being the sister taxon of Adasaurus.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested Luanchuanraptor belongs to the subfamily Averaptora, though this view is not widely accepted.
facts.quote: The genus has been considered to pertain to the Averaptora by Agnolín and Novas, but this suggestion is not widely followed.

rejected.statement: The known fossil is from an immature individual, suggesting the species grew slightly larger than the preserved specimen.
rejected.quote: the individual 41HIII-0100 preserves an unfused frontal, meaning that it was not a fully-grown animal at the time of death and therefore, they reached slightly larger sizes.
